tools.name: find_replacements
tools.title: Find self-hosted replacements
tools.description: Self-hosted, open-source options for a paid tool or a goal, each with its evidence label (tested, coverage checked, or listed untested), licence, maintenance facts, a rough hosting reference where known, and the paid tool's list price with its source and read date. Give paid_tool (for example 'zapier') or goal.

paid_tool.description: The paid product you use, for example zapier or notion.

goal.description: What the tool is for, when no paid tool is named.

tools.name: get_cost_scenarios
tools.title: List-price cost of paid tools
tools.description: The list-price monthly cost of up to five paid tools at a seat count, from each vendor's own pricing page, with how each figure was made, its read date, and the tools that have no figure and why. Every figure is an example at list price, not a quote: it leaves out discounts, taxes, add-ons, migration and hosting.

paid_tools.description: Paid tools by name or slug, for example ["notion", "slack"].

cadence.description: Billing period; default annual, as on the calculator page.

tools.name: get_finding
tools.title: Read a BenchLytix finding
tools.description: One published BenchLytix finding as structured data with its sources and read dates. 001: what five AI support vendors charge per resolution and how each defines a resolution, in the vendors' own words. 002: who makes the main-branch commits of the self-hosted alternatives BenchLytix lists.

tools.name: get_agent_score
tools.title: Get an AI agent's score
tools.description: The score and its parts for one AI agent on the BenchLytix leaderboard, by slug, as its profile page shows it: the evidence basis (scores are desk assessments of the agent's published materials unless labelled otherwise), which dimensions hold a placeholder, the latest automated security scan colour and date where shown, and the leaderboard's current status.

slug.description: The agent slug, as in its profile URL /agents/<slug>.

tools.name: get_leaderboard
tools.title: List AI agents and scores
tools.description: AI agents on the BenchLytix leaderboard with their scores and evidence labels, optionally for one task category, in the leaderboard page's order, with the leaderboard's status. Scores are desk assessments of published materials unless labelled otherwise.

category.description: A task category slug; see get_categories.

tools.name: compare_agents
tools.title: Compare AI agents side by side
tools.description: Two to five AI agents side by side, by slug, each with its score as its profile shows it, its evidence basis and which dimensions hold a placeholder. Side by side only: BenchLytix does not choose between them.

annotations.title: Compare AI agents side by side

tools.name: verify_agent
tools.title: Check whether an agent is listed
tools.description: Whether an AI agent is listed and verified on BenchLytix, by slug or by the agent's runtime-platform id (not the BenchLytix id), with its score and evidence label when it is. Give exactly one of slug or agent_id.

agent_id.description: The UUID the agent's runtime platform assigned it.

annotations.title: Check whether an agent is listed

tools.name: get_categories
tools.title: List task categories
tools.description: The task categories of the BenchLytix AI agent leaderboard, with a link to each category view. Use a slug as the category of get_leaderboard.

tools.name: get_methodology
tools.title: Read the scoring methodology summary
tools.description: How BenchLytix scores AI agents (four dimensions and their weights, the evidence labels) and how it labels self-hosted replacement options, with the methodology version, its revision and links to the full document.

tools.name: check_repo
tools.title: Check a GitHub repository
tools.description: Public facts about one GitHub repository, read from GitHub's API with their dates and sources: licence, archived state, last push, latest commit on the default branch, stars, contributors, latest release, who made the default branch's commits in the last 52 weeks, and README sentences that match a maintenance phrase list. If BenchLytix lists the repository, adds its desk-assessment score, evidence basis, scan colour and date, and the leaderboard's status. It does not judge the code.

repo.description: The repository as owner/repo, or its github.com URL (for example n8n-io/n8n or https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n).
